consensus_summary: Consensus holds a dual but mutually reinforcing primary identification of fish as (1) people/souls/converts gathered into the kingdom via the 'fishers of men' call and dragnet parable, and (2) Christ himself (plus Christian identity) via the early ICHTHYS acrostic; secondary meanings include provision, Jonah typology, Eucharist, and judgment.
book_summary: Fish symbolize men in the sea of nations, and the redeemed drawn out of it as the catch of the fishers of men gathered in the net.
consensus_core_identification: People (souls/converts) gathered by evangelism/mission into the kingdom, and/or Christ via ICHTHYS.
book_core_identification: Men of the nations (in the sea), specifically the redeemed drawn out as the catch of the fishers of men.
boundary_disagreement: Book preserves the people-as-fish category from the fishers-of-men and net texts but narrows it to 'men in the sea of nations' and exclusively the redeemed catch, while omitting the co-primary ICHTHYS/Christ referent and the full good/bad separation of the dragnet.
material_contradiction: None; book does not deny or replace the traditional Christ/ICHTHYS identification, it simply does not address it.
rationale: The book's core matches the well-attested exegetical strand in every consensus response (people as the catch of evangelism and the net). It refines rather than matches by adding the Habakkuk-linked 'sea of nations' framing and by restricting emphasis to the redeemed drawn out (a precision/boundary change that treats the catch as the good fish only). The ICHTHYS strand is left unmentioned, producing a narrowed extension of the people category without core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus responses frequently rank the ICHTHYS/Christ meaning as primary or co-equal (especially in tradition/iconography), so omitting it entirely could be viewed by some as replacing rather than merely narrowing the core referent.
